correctness.rationale: For W=im(P), rank(MP)=dim W−dim(W∩ker M). Conditional on the entire past the kernel is a uniform line, so the chance that it belongs to W is (q^r−1)/(q^n−1); the argument works in all characteristics and with nonidentical factor laws. Successive conditional geometric waiting laws have no dependence on entrance history, giving independent holding times, the PGF and the moments. The survival PGF is (1−E[z^T])/(1−z). At each nonzero pole multiplying by 1−λ_j z gives the claimed coefficient; the constant at z=∞ is ∏_{r<n}p_r/(p_r−1), the j=n coefficient. Thus the zero-base convention is correct even at k=0 and the first step is deterministic. The leading finite coefficient telescopes. On scaling by q^n−1, fixed levels converge jointly to independent exponentials, and the expected omitted tail is bounded by ∑_{r>R}1/(q^r−1); the summable squared rates inverses justify the variance limit. For a=q−1 and W the independent limiting remainder, e^{at}P(E_1+W>t)=E[e^{a min(W,t)}]; its monotone limit is the telescoping product q/(q−1). Conjugation invariance of both example classes gives uniform kernel lines, not equality of full products. The frozen check.py and log were inspected, not run; exact small-prime-field checks are corroboration, not the argument for extension fields or the limit.

value.rationale: Kernel universality lets a researcher substitute nilpotent, idempotent or mixed independent factors without changing rank trajectories, although full matrix laws differ. The exact absorption tail, including the finite leading coefficient and the fixed-field large-dimension exponential-sum law, provides usable quantitative information beyond a two-factor census or an expectation. The value is this structural invariance and quantitative stopping law, not the general partial-fraction method.
